title: Scalable Model Merging with Progressive Layer-wise Distillation

source_version.publication: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR volume 267 (2025)
source_version.version_basis: official publisher linked PDF acquired on retrieval date, frozen by SHA-256

inspection_outcome: Three verified current-release defects; historical experiment impact remains Needs Evidence
summary: The central hardness proofs check out in their explicit scope. Released NLU teacher initialization, file lifecycle, and NLG calibration exclusion contain demonstrable static defects. No historical benchmark invalidity or score change was established.

problems.title: NLU teacher prefixes use the final task rather than each task
problems.claim: Algorithm1 uses each expert's own prefix features
assumptions: Functional effect depends on whether task prefixes differ
problems.check: Parent complete source reads, static AST name binding, independent scalar expression example
problems.result: Loop binds dataset but loader reads global dataset_name=rte; later layers remain task-specific
problems.counterevidence: Identical prefix transformations would neutralize the error; actual checkpoints and historical code binding absent
problems.impact: Released teacher stream can differ from Algorithm1; historical scores not established wrong

correction.statement: Load the current dataset variable and regenerate caches
correction.limits: No repaired neural run or accuracy measurement

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The NLU loop binds dataset but loads teacher prefixes through global dataset_name, whose final value is rte. Later blocks are loaded by individual task. The static path therefore yields B_i(E_RTE(x)) where B_i(E_i(x)) is intended when prefixes differ.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The effect is conditional on differing checkpoint prefixes, and the released entrypoint is not bound to the historical runs.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor is retained for the verified release teacher-prefix selection defect, without extrapolating an unverified core historical performance effect.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: Use the loop's task identifier consistently for prefix loading; actual checkpoint equivalence and corrected scores remain unverified.

problems.title: Vision save and NLU cleanup paths block documented entrypoints
assumptions: Ordinary parser and setup without unpublished edits
problems.check: Independent PurePosixPath comparison and AST option/tag inspection
problems.result: Vision saves under ViT-B-32100 while create/load use ViT-B-32/100; NLU reads undefined args.tag
problems.counterevidence: Unpublished corrected scripts could generate paper tables; no historical linkage established
problems.impact: Current entrypoints cannot complete their intended lifecycle in the described ordinary setup

correction.statement: Use one shared path construction and remove undefined cleanup component
correction.limits: No author code execution or full training verification

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The Vision creation/loading paths contain /ViT-B-32/100/, while the save expression concatenates /ViT-B-32100/. The NLU cleanup uses args.tag although the inspected parser/setup do not define it. These are static entrypoint defects.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: Alternative scripts or historical code could have produced the published results. The check does not establish that those runs used the defective release paths.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor is retained for the bounded release file-workflow failures; the abstract distillation method is not invalidated by these path errors.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The path construction and cleanup argument should be made consistent; no author entrypoint was executed and no successful historical rerun is claimed.

problems.title: NLG calibration prompts are not consistently excluded
problems.outcome: Verified release protocol defect; historical score impact unknown
problems.claim: B3 excludes NLG calibration test examples from evaluation
problems.location: B3p18; NLG loader57–60; eval_instruct64–78,119; eval_code163–179; merge_gen8–18; README61–71
assumptions: Same Alpaca JSON used by calibration/evaluation and nonempty instruct calibration
MBPP consecutive excluded IDs are a logical diagnostic, not asserted actual membership
problems.check: Complete instruction generation-to-scorer-input trace, saved-index path, manual list-iterator counterexample
problems.result: Alpaca full JSON is generated and concatenated without index filtering; MBPP in-place deletion can skip an excluded neighbor
problems.counterevidence: Intended exclusion is disclosed; calibration uses inputs not answer labels; historical outputs/indices not available
problems.impact: Released evaluation does not enforce claimed holdout; no measured inflation or corrected scores asserted

correction.statement: Filter from saved remainder IDs into fresh list; assert disjointness and fail on missing indices
correction.limits: Actual saved dataset memberships, model outputs and scorer runs unavailable

focused_acceptance.source_location: B3p18; NLG loader57–60; eval_instruct64–78,119; eval_code163–179; merge_gen8–18; README61–71
focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The calibration loader samples the Alpaca evaluation JSON, but eval_instruct generates the full same JSON and the downstream merge/scoring path does not apply saved remaining indices. MBPP eval_code mutates task_ids with pop while iterating, which skips adjacent removable entries. The paper explicitly promises calibration-item exclusion.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: Calibration uses inputs rather than answer labels, so this does not prove answer leakage. Historical scoring bindings and any score effect are unestablished.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor is retained for the demonstrated released exclusion-protocol defect; the report preserves the narrower evidence boundary.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: Filter evaluation IDs explicitly and non-mutatively using the saved calibration partition. No corrected benchmark score is asserted.
